issues.t: Rotary engine loses compression
issues.sym: Hard starting, especially when the engine is warm, a rough idle, misfires and a gradual loss of power. Eventually the car may not start at all.
issues.why: The rotary engine's apex seals and rotor housings wear, so one or both rotors lose compression. Low oil and lots of short trips speed this up. Many cars needed a replacement engine between about 60,000 and 100,000 miles. Mazda once extended the engine core warranty on 2004-2008 cars to 8 years or 100,000 miles, but that coverage has now run out.
issues.next: Before buying or repairing, get a rotary-specific compression test (a normal piston-engine tester won't give a valid reading). If compression is low, the fix is a rebuilt or replacement engine, so compare quotes from rotary specialists.

issues.t: Engine floods and won't start after a short run
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't catch, often after the car was started cold and shut off after only a minute or two. You may smell fuel.
issues.why: If a cold rotary is shut off before it warms up, unburned fuel collects in the housings and soaks the plugs. Weak coils, worn plugs or low compression make flooding much more likely.
issues.next: Avoid starting the car just to move it a few feet; let it warm up before shutting it off. A shop (or the owner's manual de-flood procedure) can clear it. If it keeps flooding, check the plugs, coils, battery and compression.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure and misfires
issues.sym: Flashing or steady check engine light, sputtering, a rough idle, loss of power under load, and harder starting.
issues.why: The RX-8's ignition coils and plug wires wear out much sooner than on a normal engine. A weak coil lets the rotary misfire, and the unburned fuel can then damage the catalytic converter.
issues.next: Don't keep driving with a flashing check engine light. Have the misfire codes read and replace weak coils, usually together with the plugs and wires.

issues.t: Clogged or failed catalytic converter
issues.sym: Loss of power, the engine feeling choked at higher revs, a check engine light, a rattling or rotten-egg smell from the exhaust, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Misfires and flooding send raw fuel into the converter, which overheats and can melt or break up inside.
issues.next: Fix any misfire first, or a new converter will fail too. Have exhaust back pressure checked and replace the converter if it is blocked.

issues.t: Oil loss that damages the rotary engine
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, a low oil pressure warning, or a puddle of oil under the front of the car.
issues.why: A rotary engine burns some oil on purpose to lubricate its seals, so the level falls even on a healthy car. Corroded oil cooler lines can also start leaking. Running low on oil overheats the seals and is a common cause of engine failure.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and top it up as needed. If you see oil leaking near the front of the engine, have the oil cooler lines inspected right away.

issues.t: Weak starter and hot no-start
issues.sym: The engine turns over slowly or not at all, especially when it's hot, or you only hear a click.
issues.why: A rotary needs strong cranking speed to start. Starters and batteries that are getting weak, plus heat soak around the starter, leave the engine cranking too slowly to fire.
issues.next: Test the battery and cables first, since a weak battery causes the same symptoms. If they are good, replace the starter.

issues.t: Hesitation from stuck intake shutter valve
issues.sym: The car stumbles or feels flat around 5,000 to 7,000 rpm, sometimes with a check engine light (codes such as P2070 or P0661).
issues.why: Valves in the intake manifold (the secondary shutter valve and related solenoids and actuators) can stick from carbon buildup or have a failed solenoid, so the engine can't breathe properly at higher revs.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning and freeing the valve, or replacing a solenoid or actuator, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Coolant level warning and overheating
issues.sym: The coolant level light comes on, the temperature gauge rises, or coolant is lost from the reservoir.
issues.why: Thermostats that stick closed, a faulty coolant level sensor, and a leaking expansion tank or cap can all cause trouble. Mazda issued a service bulletin about the coolant level warning. Overheating is especially bad for a rotary engine.
issues.next: Stop if the gauge climbs. Have the cooling system pressure tested and the sensor checked. Don't ignore it, because overheating can ruin the engine.

issues.t: Broken engine mounts
issues.sym: Heavy vibration at idle, a clunk when shifting or getting on and off the throttle, and the engine rocking more than normal.
issues.why: The rubber in the engine and transmission mounts cracks and collapses with age.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. Replace any that are cracked or sagging; badly broken mounts can strain hoses and the exhaust.

issues.t: Fuel leak from fuel pump seals and pipe (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of gasoline inside or near the car, especially after driving, or wetness around the fuel tank under the rear seat.
issues.why: Heat from the exhaust can wear out the fuel pump's sealing rings, and a fuel pump pipe can crack. Either can leak fuel and cause a fire. Mazda recalled these years (NHTSA 16V-793 and 17V-354).
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive the car; have it towed. Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers replace the seals and pipe and add a heat shield for free.

issues.t: Fuel leak at fuel pump mounting ring (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of gasoline, especially after a drive, or fuel wetness near the top of the tank.
issues.why: Exhaust heat can wear out the fuel pump's mounting ring and seals, letting fuel leak and creating a fire risk. Mazda recalled these years (NHTSA 21V-744).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers fit new mounting rings and an insulation pad for free. If you smell fuel, have the car towed rather than driven.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Hard starting, stalling or sputtering under load, or the engine cranking but not starting.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump on the RX-8 is one of the more commonly replaced parts, and heat near the tank adds wear.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing parts. Also make sure the fuel leak recall for your year has been done.

issues.t: Takata driver air bag can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The danger appears only when the air bag deploys in a crash.
issues.why: The driver's air bag inflator can be damaged by moisture over time and burst when it deploys, throwing metal fragments. Mazda recalled these cars (NHTSA 17V-474) and has told owners of unrepaired cars not to drive them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls right away. If the recall is open, don't drive the car; have it towed to a Mazda dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: Takata passenger air bag can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning. The danger appears only when the passenger air bag deploys in a crash.
issues.why: The passenger air bag inflator can explode and throw metal fragments into the cabin. These cars were covered by several recalls (NHTSA 18V-402, 18V-403, 19V-488 and 19V-781).
issues.next: Look up the VIN for open recalls. If one is open, have the car towed to a dealer for the free replacement and don't carry a front passenger until it is fixed.

issues.t: Front lower ball joint can separate (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front suspension over bumps and steering that feels loose. If the joint comes apart, the wheel can lose steering control.
issues.why: The socket holding the ball joint in the front lower control arm can crack, especially with hard driving. Mazda recalled 2004 cars twice for this (NHTSA 05V-325 and 17V-355); the fix is new lower control arms.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls. If you hear front-end clunks, have the ball joints inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Engine heat damage and fuel leak at high rpm (recall)
issues.sym: Possible fuel smell or engine running problems after sustained high-rpm driving; often no warning before the fault.
issues.why: Mazda found that long periods at very high engine speed could cause heat damage that leads to a fuel leak and a fire risk (NHTSA 05V-317, about 52,000 early cars).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and make sure it was completed. If you ever smell fuel, park the car and have it inspected.

issues.t: Transmission heat insulator can crack and fall off (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or scraping from under the car, or a piece of heat shield hanging down.
issues.why: A heat insulator near the transmission could crack and come loose, becoming a road hazard for cars behind (NHTSA 04V-075).
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you hear rattling or dragging from underneath, have the underside inspected.

issues.t: Electric power steering loss or jerky steering
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, a power steering warning light comes on, or the steering jerks or feels notchy while turning.
issues.why: The RX-8 uses electric power steering. Faults in the steering motor, its control unit or low system voltage can switch the assist off or make it uneven.
issues.next: Grip the wheel firmly and slow down if assist drops out. Test the battery and charging system, then have the steering system scanned for codes.

issues.t: Climate control unit fails to adjust temperature
issues.sym: The heat or A/C won't change temperature when you turn the knob, the display is faulty, or the controls stop responding.
issues.why: The climate control panel and head unit fail on these cars, so they can no longer control the system properly.
issues.next: Have the HVAC system checked to rule out a blend door motor. If the control unit is at fault, it needs to be replaced.

issues.t: Clutch pedal and hydraulic problems
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft, sticks to the floor, or the car grinds going into gear. Some owners hear a whine from the release bearing.
issues.why: On manual cars, the clutch master cylinder, the pedal pivot and linkage, and the release bearing wear out more often than usual.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid level and look for leaks. A shop can tell whether the master cylinder, linkage or clutch itself needs replacing.

issues.t: Water inside the tail lights
issues.sym: Fog, water droplets or standing water inside the rear light lenses.
issues.why: The tail light seals let moisture in. Water can eventually corrode the bulb sockets.
issues.next: Have the light units resealed or replaced. Check the bulbs and sockets for corrosion while you're at it.

issues.t: Alternator failure
issues.sym: Battery or charging light on, dimming lights, or a battery that keeps going flat.
issues.why: The alternator is among the RX-8's common replacement parts. A weak charging system also makes starting and steering assist problems worse.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Replace the alternator if output is low.

issues.t: Power window regulator or motor failure
issues.sym: A window moves slowly, stops partway, makes grinding noises, or drops into the door.
issues.why: The window regulators and motor gears wear and break.
issues.next: Have the door opened up and the regulator or motor replaced.
